competitors.name: WP Mail SMTP
competitors.oneLiner: The most-installed SMTP plugin. Free sending; logs, backup and alerts are in Pro.
competitors.verdict: WP Mail SMTP is the default choice for a reason: 4 million sites, a 4.8-star rating from more than 5,000 reviews, and 19 years on WordPress.org. Its free version sends email well, but the email log, backup connection, failure alerts and Amazon SES or Microsoft 365 sending are all in Pro, from $99 a year at full price. VuloMail includes those in the free plugin and adds SMS alerts, but it is brand new and has no reviews yet.
competitors.freeTier: Sending through 14 email services or any SMTP server, Gmail sign-in, test emails and a domain DNS check.

plans.name: Elite
plans.note: Adds White Glove Setup. $99 in the first year

competitors.pricingNote: Discounts are introductory; WP Mail SMTP states that renewals are at full price.

failAlerts.note: Email, Slack, Teams, Discord, Twilio SMS, webhooks

theyWin: Track record: 4 million active installs and 5,205 reviews averaging 4.8 out of 5. VuloMail was listed on 12 October 2026 and has no reviews yet.
Sign in with Google in the free version, so no Gmail password or app password is stored on your site. VuloMail's Gmail preset uses an app password.
Pro has features VuloMail doesn't offer at any price: open and click tracking, weekly email summaries, rate limiting, background sending queues, conditional routing and multisite network settings.
Paid one-to-one support and a White Glove Setup service that configures DNS and the mailer for you.
weWin: Email log, resend, backup connection and failure alerts are free in VuloMail. In WP Mail SMTP each needs Pro, $99 a year for one site at full price.
Amazon SES, Microsoft 365 and Zoho presets are in the free plugin, alongside 22 email APIs. WP Mail SMTP keeps all three for Pro.

SMS: WooCommerce order, stock and review alerts for you, and order updates for customers, through Twilio, Vonage, Plivo or Clickatell. WP Mail SMTP only texts you when an email fails, and only in Pro.

No outside service in the loop: VuloMail's DNS check runs from your own server, and it never contacts a VuloLabs server. WP Mail SMTP's domain check sends your From address and domain to its own service.
chooseThem: You want the most proven plugin and the largest support community.
You need open and click tracking, weekly reports, rate limiting or multisite network controls, and you're happy to pay for Pro.
You send through Gmail and want Google sign-in instead of an app password.
chooseUs: You want a log, a backup connection and failure alerts without a yearly licence.
You run WooCommerce and want texts about orders and stock, or order updates sent to customers.
You use one of the less common services VuloMail supports, such as ZeptoMail, SocketLabs, Mailtrap or Bird.

competitors.name: FluentSMTP
competitors.oneLiner: Fully free, with no Pro version: OAuth, logs, fallback, alerts and WP-CLI included.
competitors.verdict: FluentSMTP is VuloMail's closest match and a genuinely strong plugin: completely free, with a log, a fallback connection, failure alerts, Google and Microsoft sign-in and WP-CLI. If you only need email, it does more than VuloMail does today. VuloMail's difference is SMS: store and customer texts for WooCommerce, alongside a wider list of email services and privacy-first defaults.
competitors.freeTier: Everything. FluentSMTP has no paid version and says it never will.
competitors.pricingNote: No paid plans. WPManageNinja has pledged FluentSMTP as part of its Five for the Future contribution.

services.note: 14 API connections, including Cloudflare and toSend

log.note: Full headers, body and server response

theyWin: Sign in with Google and Microsoft (OAuth), so no mailbox password is stored. VuloMail's Gmail and Microsoft presets use app passwords.
Failure alerts to Telegram, Slack, Discord and Pushover, plus a daily health check of every connection.
Route different From addresses to different providers, and manage it all from WP-CLI.
Option to keep credentials in wp-config.php instead of the database.
A five-year track record: 700,000 active installs and 407 reviews averaging 4.8 out of 5.
weWin: SMS is built in: 18 alerts for your site and WooCommerce store, including order updates texted to customers. FluentSMTP has no SMS at all.
More email services: 22 email APIs and 18 SMTP presets, including Mailjet, MailerSend, Mailtrap, Mandrill, Resend, SendLayer, ZeptoMail, SocketLabs and SendPulse, which FluentSMTP doesn't list.
Privacy defaults: message bodies aren't stored unless you opt in, recipients can be masked, and old entries prune themselves after 30 days.
If both connections fail, WordPress's own mailer can still try as a last resort, and every attempt appears on a single log row.
A sender-domain check for SPF and DMARC records in Diagnostics.
chooseThem: You only need email, and want Google or Microsoft sign-in, WP-CLI or Slack and Telegram alerts.
You want to route different senders to different providers.
chooseUs: You also want SMS alerts, or texts to WooCommerce customers, without adding a second plugin.
Your provider is one FluentSMTP doesn't support natively, such as Mailjet, Resend or ZeptoMail.
You'd rather not store email bodies, which can contain password-reset links, by default.

competitors.verdict: Site Mailer (now called Email Deliverability) works differently from every other plugin here: instead of connecting your own email provider, it sends through Elementor's service and needs an Elementor account. The free plan covers 200 emails in total, not per month. It is rated 2.5 out of 5 from 17 reviews. VuloMail is a free connector for a provider you choose and pay directly.

VuloMail does far more, still for free.
